setupDisplay.notes: Requests missing a required field for their state are rejected with {ok:false}. progress must be a finite number. The player renders overlay-driving commands (mintPairingDisplay, setupDisplay) without arbitration, so the controller must keep at most one non-hidden at a time.

renderStatus.notes: checkStatus replies carry an optional numeric renderStatus: 0 pending, 1 loading, 2 ready, 3 failed. Live-only — never persisted, so boot and hydrate strip it. `ready` means the artwork finished loading AND is what the screen is showing, not that it rendered correctly. It publishes when the incoming slot commits, so on a transition it trails byte arrival by up to the crossfade duration (650ms); a first load publishes immediately. For iframe/PDF a browser-generated error document still reports ready, because Chromium does not emit an iframe error for a failed navigation. On a player build that declares this entry, an ABSENT renderStatus means 'no lifecycle published yet for the current mount' — not a terminal state, and not a fault. A manifest without this entry is an older build that never reports the field at all: controld must treat that as capability-absent rather than as a stuck pending, because the two are byte-identical on the wire (JSON.stringify drops the undefined key).

playerStatus.notes: window.__ffosPlayerStatus() (no request payload — a plain global function, not a checkStatus-style command) returns JSON.stringify({protocol, route, handlerRegistered, hasArtwork, bootHydration}), where bootHydration is one of pending|ok|halted_cleared|halted_preserving|failed. Installed by CDPRequestHandler.initialize() and set back to null by cleanup(). Absent on player builds that predate this contract entry — controld's capability fuse treats a manifest without this entry as unsupported and falls back to conservative (log-only) boot recovery.
